    • A mizer model with von Bertalanffy growth

Create model with von Bertalanffy growth rates in the steady state

Source: R/newVonBertalanffyParams.R
newVonBertalanffyParams.Rd

Builds a single- or multi-species MizerParams object in which each species grows along its von Bertalanffy curve while at steady state. The von Bertalanffy parameters are supplied in the w_inf, k_vb and t0 columns of species_params, together with the weight-length exponent b, the maturity size w_mat and the maximum size w_max.

Usage

newVonBertalanffyParams(species_params, no_w = 200, max_w = NULL)

Arguments

species_params

Species parameter data frame. Must contain the von Bertalanffy parameters w_inf, k_vb and t0 as well as the usual mizer parameters such as b, w_mat and w_max.

no_w

Number of size bins. Default 200

max_w

Largest size in the model. Defaults to the largest w_max.

Value

A MizerParams object with the model at steady state

Growth

The von Bertalanffy growth in length, \(dl/dt = k_{vb}(L_\infty - l)\), becomes in weight \(dw/dt = A\,w^n - B\,w\) with \(n = 1 - 1/b\), \(A = b\,k_{vb}\,w_\infty^{1/b}\) and \(B = b\,k_{vb}\) (see vonBertalanffyGrowth()). The model reproduces this rate by

  • switching off satiation, predation and resource interactions so that the energy income is a pure power law \(\alpha E = A\,w^n\),

  • setting the metabolic loss rate to \(B\,w\) (so \(\alpha E - \mathrm{metab} = A\,w^n - B\,w\)), and

  • switching off constant mortality and using a power-law external mortality chosen to give the juvenile biomass density a slight negative slope.

Reproduction

Mizer computes somatic growth as \(g = (1 - \psi)(\alpha E - \mathrm{metab})\), where \(\psi\) is the fraction of surplus energy invested into reproduction. For the somatic growth to stay on the von Bertalanffy curve the surplus energy must therefore be \(g_{vb}/(1 - \psi)\), so the metabolic loss is reduced by \(\psi/(1 - \psi)\,g_{vb}\). Because w_repro_max is set to w_inf, and mizer's maturity ogive gives \(\psi \propto (w/w_{\mathrm{repro\,max}})^{1-n}\) above w_mat, this reduction equals the metabolic loss across the mature range where the ogive has saturated (reducing the metabolic loss to zero there, so the income funds both somatic growth and reproduction) and is smaller in the maturation transition just above w_mat; either way it never exceeds the metabolic loss, which therefore stays non-negative.

Negative t0

A negative t0 means the von Bertalanffy fish already has a positive size at age 0, so mizer, which starts every fish at w_min, cannot follow the curve below maturity. Instead a speed-up \(\Delta(w) = s\,w^n(1 - (w/w_{\mathrm{mat}})^{1-n})\) is added to the growth rate below maturity, chosen so that maturity is reached at the age the von Bertalanffy curve (with its negative t0) predicts, namely \(t_{\mathrm{mat}} = t_0 - \log(1 - (w_{\mathrm{mat}}/w_\infty)^{1/b})/k_{vb}\). Because \(\Delta\) vanishes at w_mat, the growth rate stays continuous there, and above maturity the growth is unchanged and so coincides with the von Bertalanffy curve.

Since \(g_{vb} + \Delta = (A + s)\,w^n - (B + s/w_{\mathrm{mat}}^{1/b})\,w\) is again of von Bertalanffy form, the age to maturity has a closed form which is inverted for the amplitude \(s\). Its \(w^n\) term is added to the encounter rate (income) and its \(w\) term to the metabolic loss, keeping consumption allometric (\(\propto w^n\)) and respiration linear (\(\propto w\)). A message notes that juvenile intake is raised for the affected species. An error is raised only if t0 is so negative that \(t_{\mathrm{mat}} \le 0\). Species with t0 >= 0 (or missing t0) are left unchanged.
